why_next: This experiment falsifies token savings for short-value URL patterns (-6.4% mean, parameterized uses MORE tokens) but the resolve/bind pipeline is validated. The product economics question remains open on two orthogonal paths: (1) long-value patterns where template syntax overhead is dominated by concrete values, or (2) amortized deduplication benefit where fewer unique mechanisms offset per-mechanism token penalty. A discriminating test on long values is cheaper and more informative than full amortized economics. However, the Fix3 independent-necessity question from parent EXP-PRODUCT-35185290656 remains open and could be pursued simultaneously by the graph lane.
